chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'To gift my Muslim brother a gift that benefits him is more beloved to me than to give in charity an equivalent amount.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Why is gifting a brother more beloved than charity in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elevates the act of giving a specific, beneficial gift (hibah) over general charity (sadaqah), emphasizing the relational and social bonds strengthened by personal attention. This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'silat al-rahim' (maintaining kinship/friendship ties) as a means of preserving dignity and fostering mutual love, rather than merely fulfilling a financial obligation. It underscores that targeted generosity serves as a stronger mechanism for social cohesion and spiritual connection than impersonal almsgiving.
